sql: Orders contains (customer_id, amount): (1,10), (1,20), (2,5). What does SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id return?
GROUP BY creates one group per customer and SUM adds amounts within each group.
A table has x values 10, NULL, 20. What are COUNT(*) and COUNT(x)?
COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(x) excludes NULL values.
Customers A and B exist. Only A has two orders. How many rows does a LEFT JOIN from customers to orders return, with no filters?
A produces two matching rows; B produces one row with NULL order columns.
Which clause filters groups whose SUM(amount) exceeds 100 after aggregation?
HAVING filters aggregate groups; WHERE filters input rows before aggregation.
Events have a stable event_id. Duplicate imports repeat the same event_id, but different events can have equal timestamps. Which key best identifies duplicate events?
The stable event identifier distinguishes legitimate events with equal timestamps.
statistics-fundamentals: For values 2, 3, 3, 4, 100, what are the mean and median?
20 and 4
The sum is 112, so the mean is 22.4; the middle sorted value is 3.
Two datasets have the same mean. One has a larger standard deviation. What does that indicate?
Its mean must be wrong
It contains more rows
It has a higher median
Its values are more dispersed around the mean
Standard deviation measures dispersion, not sample size or the median.
A satisfaction survey is sent only to customers who renewed. What is the main concern when estimating satisfaction of all customers?
Selection bias from excluding non-renewers
Renewal guarantees a representative sample
The mean cannot be calculated
All responses must be false
Renewal can be related to satisfaction, so excluding non-renewers changes the target population represented.
A conversion estimate rises from 20 successes in 100 independent trials to 200 in 1000, with similar sampling conditions. What usually happens to sampling uncertainty?
It must increase tenfold
It generally decreases
It becomes exactly zero
It is determined only by the numerator
At the same estimated proportion, a larger independent sample generally reduces the standard error.
A diagnostic test has 90% sensitivity. Which statement follows directly?
90% of positive results are true cases
90% of all people have the condition
90% of people with the condition test positive
The false-positive rate is 10%
Sensitivity conditions on having the condition; positive predictive value also depends on prevalence and specificity.
data-cleaning: An age field contains -5, 25, and 40. Ages must be non-negative. What is the most defensible first action?
Replace -5 with 0 automatically
Delete the entire table
Assume -5 is a valid age
Flag -5 and investigate the source before choosing a correction
Validation identifies an impossible value; correction needs evidence about its intended value.
Order rows repeat because of an import error. A unique order_id is available. What should guide deduplication?
The documented order_id uniqueness rule
Delete every row sharing a customer
Keep only the largest order
Round all amounts
A documented business key distinguishes duplicate orders from multiple legitimate orders by one customer.
Income is missing much more often for high-income respondents. What is unsafe to assume?
The missingness pattern should be investigated
The missing values are a completely random subset
An imputation method needs justification
Sensitivity analysis may be useful
Observed dependence on income conflicts with treating missingness as completely random.
A pipeline receives dates 03/04/2026 from sources using both DD/MM and MM/DD. What is safest?
Always use the machine locale
Sort the text and infer the format
Parse using each source's documented format
Replace all dates with today's date
The date is ambiguous without source-specific format information.
A valid transaction is far larger than the rest. What should happen before removing it as an outlier?
Remove it because it affects the mean
Replace it with the median without logging
Delete all large transactions
Check provenance and whether it belongs to the analysis population
An unusual value can be genuine; removal must follow the analysis purpose and documented rules.
data-visualization: Which chart is usually most suitable for monthly revenue over two years?
A line chart with ordered months
A pie chart with 24 slices
A map without geographic data
An unordered word cloud
A line chart preserves temporal ordering and supports trend inspection.
A bar chart compares 98 and 100 with a vertical axis beginning at 97. What is the main risk?
It hides the category names automatically
It exaggerates the visual difference in bar lengths
It changes the underlying values
It guarantees a causal conclusion
Bar lengths encode magnitude, so a truncated baseline can exaggerate differences.
Which plot best shows the distribution and skew of a numeric variable?
A pie chart of row numbers
A network diagram
A histogram with justified bin widths
A decorative gauge
A histogram summarizes frequencies across numeric intervals and reveals distribution shape.
Two groups have similar point estimates but wide confidence intervals. What should a chart show?
Only the larger estimate
Only a red or green winner label
A claim that the groups are equal
The estimates and their uncertainty intervals
Intervals communicate uncertainty that point estimates alone conceal.
A sales chart combines amounts in USD and EUR without conversion. What must be addressed before comparing heights?
Convert to a common currency using a stated basis or separate the units clearly
Use a brighter color
Remove the legend
Sort alphabetically
Comparable magnitudes require compatible units and a stated conversion basis.
data-analysis: Ice cream sales and drowning incidents rise together in summer. What conclusion is justified from this observation alone?
Ice cream causes drowning
They are associated; season may be a confounder
Drowning causes all ice cream sales
There is no possible third variable
Association alone cannot establish causality; temperature or season can affect both variables.
Campaign A has 20 purchases from 100 visits and B has 30 from 300. Which has the higher observed conversion rate?
B at 30%
They are both 20%
A at 20%, compared with B at 10%
B because it has more purchases
Conversion rates use purchases divided by visits, not purchase counts alone.
An overall conversion rate improves while rates within both device groups decline. What should be investigated?
Assume the data are impossible
Delete device categories
Conclude every group improved
Changes in the proportions of traffic across device groups
Changing group composition can reverse an aggregate comparison, as in Simpson's paradox.
Before estimating whether a new onboarding flow improves retention, what should be specified first?
The retention definition, population, observation window, and comparison design
The desired positive result
Only a dashboard color
A rule to exclude all users who leave
A defined estimand and comparison design make the analysis interpretable and reduce selective reporting.
A classifier is evaluated on records used to fit it. What is the main concern?
Training data always contain no signal
Performance may be optimistic compared with unseen data
Accuracy becomes a causal effect
A larger chart fixes the problem
Training-set evaluation does not provide an independent estimate of generalization performance.
